01 About me

Working where policy
meets institutions.

My career began in public interest law and grew through election observation, civic space programming, and institutional leadership. Across these roles, I’ve worked on how democratic institutions function, how citizens participate, and how evidence can inform better decisions.

That work has involved leading teams, managing budgets and donor relationships, coordinating programmes, and contributing to research on election finance, voter behaviour, and governance.

I hold a Master of Public Policy and Management from Kathmandu University. I’m particularly interested in the connection between policy research and the practical work of implementing, managing, and improving institutions.

Recent assignment

A three-month assignment with the Social Protection Civil Society Network (SPCSN) is adding a social protection perspective to my broader governance experience.

06 How I approach the work

Understand carefully.
Communicate clearly.
Follow through.

For me, policy and programme work come together in the quality of everyday decisions: how we gather evidence, engage people, and turn plans into action.

01

Start with the evidence

Check the facts, understand the context, and make claims the information can support.

02

Make it understandable

Shape research, reports, and conversations around what people need to understand and decide.

03

Keep the next step clear

Connect analysis and discussion with responsibilities, practical actions, and follow-up.
